definitions.explanation: Of the highest moral, intellectual, or spiritual value. Describes ideals, purposes, or experiences that inspire awe and reverence.

examples.japanese: {崇高|すうこう}な{理想|りそう}を{掲|かか}げる。
{自然|しぜん}の{崇高|すうこう}な{美|うつく}しさに{心|こころ}を{打|う}たれた。
examples.english: I was struck by the sublime beauty of nature.

examples.japanese: {人命|じんめい}{救助|きゅうじょ}という{崇高|すうこう}な{使命|しめい}を{果|は}たすために{働|はたら}いている。
examples.english: They work to fulfill the noble mission of saving human lives.

notes: A literary, elevated word used for things that inspire deep respect or awe. Common collocations: {崇高|すうこう}な{精神|せいしん} (noble spirit), {崇高|すうこう}な{目的|もくてき} (lofty purpose), {崇高|すうこう}な{犠牲|ぎせい} (noble sacrifice). Not used for everyday matters — it conveys grandeur and moral weight. The related verb is {崇|あが}める (to revere, to worship).
